svg.title: Card fraud platform: deployment
svg.desc: Host tools and model servers, the Docker Desktop VM with the compose profiles above the kind cluster and its namespaces, the Azure resources of the IaC runs, and the internet services the platform uses.
svg.text: CARD FRAUD PLATFORM · DEPLOYMENT · LAYERS 1 TO 3
Deployment: one Windows host (Docker Desktop VM: compose profiles + a kind cluster), Azure for the IaC runs, SaaS on the internet
the code; Jenkins polls branch main
agent prompts, eval datasets and results
second LLM for an A/B test (off now)
built on the VM by Ansible
DOCKER DESKTOP · WSL2 VM · 8 GB RAM + 4 GB swap (.wslconfig)
pods -> lakehouse-s3:8333, kafka, ml-db, redis, mlflow, vector-db, scoring-api, drift-api (node on fraud_default)

Solid card = a container or pod that keeps running; dashed card = a one-shot job that exits; :port = published on 127.0.0.1 (compose) or a NodePort (kind); arrow = a network path, from the caller to the address it calls.
8 GB does not hold every profile: run stream alone; keep trino and dbt off while orch + gov run; Layer 3 runs with core + ml + CI/CD (profile cicd) and the kind cluster.
seaweedfs has the alias lakehouse-s3: inside kind, KFP's own seaweedfs Service shadows the short name.
The model servers run on the host GPU (GTX 1070, Pascal: no vLLM); llm-d's InferencePool selects thin bridge pods that forward to them.
Azure (docs/operations/iac.md) exists only during an IaC run: created, checked, destroyed. Its quotas (6 vCPU and 3 public IPs per region, 0 for GPUs) keep the rest of the platform on the PC.
